transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I keep messing up little things, more than I think I should. Like I’ll write the wrong time down on a senior-center class sheet, or I’ll measure a board and still cut it just a bit short because I missed some small print or skipped over a detail. It’s not huge stuff, but it keeps happening and it’s frustrating.
Have you noticed this kind of forgetfulness and attention to detail being a problem for you since childhood, or is this something that's new or has gotten worse recently?

It’s not totally new, no. I remember even back in elementary school, teachers would say I was bright, but I’d forget my books or lose homework. I’d be staring out the window unless someone kind of kept me on track. So it’s been there a long time, I think.
Do you notice yourself feeling persistently worried or anxious about these mistakes or other things, even when you're not actively working on a task?

I don’t think so, not persistently. I mean, I get frustrated when I catch a mistake, and I might think, “Oh, come on, how did I miss that?” But I’m not sitting around worrying about it all the time when I’m not doing anything.

Do you notice these lapses in attention and small mistakes happening across different areas of your life—like at home, at work, and in social situations—or does it mostly happen in just one particular setting?

It happens in more than one place, yeah. At home my wife will sometimes double-check plans because I might get a time wrong or mix up something for a family visit. And at the senior center, with the activities or DIY stuff, I’ve stepped back from helping lead a couple workshops because I was worried I’d throw something off with a small mistake.
Compared to how things were, say, 5 or 10 years ago, would you say these lapses have stayed about the same, or have they been getting noticeably worse recently?

It’s been more noticeable recently, I’d say. It really started interfering after we moved into the condo, about a year and a month ago. Before that it was there, but it didn’t seem to get in the way quite as much.

Besides these small attention-related mistakes, have you noticed any new difficulty remembering recent conversations or events, like forgetting what someone told you yesterday or misplacing recent memories?

Not really, no. I might misplace something because I wasn’t paying attention, but I haven’t noticed forgetting whole conversations or things that happened the day before. At least not in a way that feels new or different.
Do you notice yourself feeling restless, needing to move around, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

I wouldn’t say I’m especially impulsive, but I do get restless sometimes. Like if I’m sitting through a whole meeting, or even just a quiet evening at the condo, I get that ants-in-my-pants feeling. I’ll want to get up, check on something, or just putter around a bit instead of sitting still.
Since moving into the condo, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested in the morning?
I haven’t really noticed a clear change there. My sleep seems about the same to me. Some nights are better than others, but I wouldn’t say moving into the condo brought on a new sleep problem.
Since moving into the condo about a year ago, have you noticed feeling persistently down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have normal ups and downs, but I haven’t felt persistently down or like I’ve stopped enjoying things since moving into the condo.
